# Directions

The project has 5 parts, one for each topic day of Module 3 - Resample, each in its own file. This is Part A. Complete each question, including the appropriate output.
This document will be used on the exam. For any question make sure to display any requested output. If you use any AI assistance in implementing the R code, be prepared to explain how the implementation works.

Helpful hint: remember to knit the document periodically to make sure the project can be knit prior to printing out your paper copy before the exam.

# Data

Every part uses the daily record of Capital Bikeshare, the bike-sharing
system in Washington DC, for the 731 days of 2011 and 2012. Each row is a day.
`total` counts that day's rentals, split into `casual` riders and
`registered` members, and `temp` is the day's average temperature in degrees
Celsius. `data-raw/bikes.R` describes the other columns.

```{r bikes}
bikes <- read.csv("../../data/bikes.csv")
n <- nrow(bikes)
head(bikes)
```

Days are not independent. A warm week tends to follow a warm week, and
ridership grew from 2011 to 2012. Part A treats the days as independent, and
Part C comes back to this.

# Part A: The bootstrap

## A.1

(a) Write `boot_reps(d, stat, B)`, which draws `B` bootstrap samples of the
rows of the data frame `d` and returns `stat` of each. Use `sample` and
`replicate`. The statistic takes a data frame, for example
`function(d) mean(d$total)`. With $B = 2000$, compare the bootstrap SE of the
mean of `total` with $s / \sqrt n$.

(b) Plot `total` against `temp`, and compute their correlation $r$. Bootstrap
$r$ with $B = 2000$, and report the bootstrap SE and the normal, basic and
percentile 95% intervals.

## A.2

The **Gini coefficient** measures how unequal a distribution is. For a
distribution $F$ with mean $\mu$, and $X$ and $Y$ independent draws from $F$,
$$G = \frac{\E{|X - Y|}}{2\mu}.$$
It is 0 when every value is the same, and it approaches 1 when a few values
are much larger than the rest. Here it measures how unevenly rentals are
spread over the days.

(a) The plug-in estimator replaces $F$ with $\hat F$, the distribution that
puts mass $1/n$ on each of $x_1, \ldots, x_n$. Show that this gives
$$\hat G = \frac{1}{2 \bar x n^2} \sum_{i=1}^n \sum_{j=1}^n |x_i - x_j|.$$
Hints: if $X$ and $Y$ are independent draws from $\hat F$, what is
$P(X = x_i, Y = x_j)$? And what is the mean of $\hat F$?

(b) Write `gini(x)`. `outer(x, x, "-")` computes every difference
$x_i - x_j$. The exponential distribution has $G = 1/2$; check `gini` on
10,000 exponential draws.

(c) Compute $\hat G$ for `casual` and for `registered`, and their difference.
Bootstrap the difference by resampling days, with $B = 2000$, and report its
SE and percentile 95% interval. Then compute the SE a second way, taking the
two Gini coefficients from two independent bootstrap samples of days. Which
SE is correct, and why is the other one larger?

## A.3

(a) A bootstrap sample draws $n$ times with replacement from $n$ days. Show
that the probability a given day is left out of the sample is
$(1 - 1/n)^n$. Recall from the "Why 63%" slide in video 1 that $(1 - 1/n)^n \to e^{-1} \approx 0.368$
as $n \to \infty$.

(b) The quietest day was October 29, 2012, when Hurricane Sandy reached
Washington, with `r min(bikes$total)` rentals. Bootstrap the minimum of
`total` with $B = 2000$. What fraction of the bootstrap minima equal
`r min(bikes$total)`, and what does (a) predict? Tabulate the values the
bootstrap minimum takes, and give the percentile 95% interval. Why does the
bootstrap fail for this statistic?
